---
title: "About"
---

A reproduction-plus-analysis study by Kacper Lisowicz, Yunzhe Zheng and Daniel Lin. Done as a research project for Hunter College's **Big Data Analytics and Applied Privacy** course.

## Reproducibility

- **Code and setup:** all code lives in the `dpdisparity` Python package. The notebooks only call it. See the repository README for setup.
- **Where results come from:**
  - Initial results from the [original testing repository](https://github.com/YunzheOVE/dp-subgroup-disparity)
  - Adult and MNIST have also been retrained with this repository's pipeline; their pages compare the two.
  - Folktables results are this repository's own (`results/folktables/`); there are no earlier runs.
- **To retrain a dataset:** `uv run python scripts/sweep.py --dataset adult` (or `mnist`; use a GPU for MNIST and Folktables).
  - Folktables: `--dataset folktables_sex` (natural sex ratio), `--dataset folktables_sex --balance`, `--dataset folktables_sex --n-train 5000 10000 25000 50000 100000` (size sweep), `--dataset folktables_race`, the $\varepsilon$ sweep `--dataset folktables_sex --n-train 25000 --methods dpsgd global_adapt --target-epsilon 0.5 1 2 8`, and the matched-learning-rate non-private baseline `--methods nonprivate --lr 0.2` (add the same `--n-train` / `--balance` / dataset options). Runs at a non-preset learning rate are stored separately (`..._lr0.2/`).
- **Folktables data:** the 2018 1-Year American Community Survey (ACS) Public Use Microdata Sample, California person file, from the US Census Bureau.
  - The [`folktables`](https://github.com/socialfoundations/folktables) package (Ding et al., 2021) downloads it from census.gov into `data/folktables/` (about 255 MB). Its SHA-256 is pinned in the loader.
  - Task: **ACSIncome**, income > \$50K from 10 features (age, class of worker, education, marital status, occupation, place of birth, relationship, hours worked, sex, race), on employed adults (age > 16, income > \$100, hours > 0). California has 195,665 such people.
  - Preprocessing follows our Adult pipeline: age and hours standardized, the other categoricals one-hot encoded (815 inputs; 805 for the white/Black subset), sex kept as an input, 80/20 seeded split.
- **Folktables privacy:** $\varepsilon$ is fixed at 3.41 (Adult's) and the noise multiplier $\sigma$ is solved for each run's sampling rate with Opacus's `get_noise_multiplier`, so runs of different sizes get the same guarantee. The solved $\sigma$ is stored with each result.
- **Hardware:** the MNIST rerun and all Folktables runs used an NVIDIA RTX 5060 Ti (CUDA 12.8, PyTorch 2.11, Opacus 1.6); exact versions are stored in every result file.
- **Hyperparameters:** Esipova et al. (2023), App. B.
- **Privacy:** Poisson sampling, RDP accountant, $\delta = 10^{-6}$. Global-Adapt's private count is included in $\varepsilon$.
- **Statistics:** values are means over 5 seeds ± standard error ($\text{SE} = \text{SD}/\sqrt{5}$), matching the paper's convention.
- **The disparity measure** is the privacy-cost gap $\lvert \operatorname{mean}(\pi_a - \pi_b) \rvert$. It is not the raw accuracy gap.

## Literature

| Paper | Role in this project |
|---|---|
| Esipova et al., *Disparate Impact in Differential Privacy from Gradient Misalignment*, ICLR 2023 | Main paper: mechanism, Global-Adapt, MNIST and Adult targets. Code: `layer6ai-labs/fair-dp` |
| Bagdasaryan et al., *Differential Privacy Has Disparate Impact on Model Accuracy*, NeurIPS 2019 | Original observation: DP-SGD hurts underrepresented groups more |
| Farrand et al., *Neither Private Nor Fair*, PPMLP 2020 | Even modest imbalance produces measurable disparity |
| Sanyal et al., *How Unfair is Private Learning?*, UAI 2022 | Part of the gap is fundamental: DP limits learning rare examples |
| Mangold et al., *Differential Privacy has Bounded Impact on Fairness in Classification*, ICML 2023 | The fairness gap from privacy is bounded and shrinks with more data; comparison point for the Folktables size sweep |
| Ding et al., *Retiring Adult: New Datasets for Fair Machine Learning*, NeurIPS 2021 | The Folktables package and the ACSIncome task, a modern, larger replacement for Adult |
| Yao & Juarez, SaTML 2025 | Survey of proposed causes of disparate impact |
| Demelius et al., TMLR 2025 | Conclusions depend on metric and hyperparameters |
